points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the captured record.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English pages without CAPTCHA. Page one contains a new Google concept page, the broad PSC overview, a MongoDB Atlas codelab, general PSC videos and vendor docs; page two starts with the exact Google configuration guide then falls into global-access news, generic PSC guides, workspace integrations and cross-cloud material.

G2=pass: the result set is documentation-heavy and fragmented; page two is a clear quality cliff outside Google's two complementary inner pages, with no exact-task media or strong-brand homepage takeover.

The concept page explains specifications, architecture, DNS and Shared VPC. The separate exact configuration page completes the task with roles, API enablement, endpoint creation, verification, private DNS, client overrides, global-access updates and deletion; it reports Last updated 2026-08-12 UTC.

G3=pass: the concept page is informational rather than a second implementation. Only the exact Google configuration page completes regional and multi-regional Google API access through PSC. The MongoDB codelab and vendor pages target different managed services.
This is not veto_window_bet because no second independent exact implementation is merely awaiting indexing.
Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. The concept and implementation pages are newly dated August 12, while adjacent global-access and generic PSC material can close the gap quickly.

Invalidation conditions: two free independent end-to-end multi-regional Google API endpoint guides enter the SERP; Google publishes a second exact codelab; supported endpoint specifications, Shared VPC roles, DNS flow, or gcloud creation syntax changes.
